title: Mouthpieces: Myers and grinding the lay
summary: He has used only three mouthpieces in his life, now a medium-lay Myers, and never ground the lay as some New Orleans players did.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: In regard to the mouthpiece, do you have a favorite make of a mouthpiece?

No, no. I tell you what I have in business. I've been playing kind of, I think I only used three mouthpieces in my whole life. You get a lot of guys that paint these, especially saxophone, the red instrument. Some companies put out all kind of mouthpieces, you know. And they look like they have trouble finding a good mouthpiece to work it. So what they do, everything come out, they buy it. So they don't get used to one before they buy another one. And your mouthpiece is very limited to 50% of your paint. If you've got a good weed and a good mouthpiece, you don't have to worry about that anymore. They don't want to squeak. You don't want to play music. You play what you want and all you know it's coming out.
This one on here is a CG-com, that mouthpiece. I wonder, is that the same kind you have?

No, I'm using myers. Myers, I see. It just happened to, the last one I had, my client fell off the chair. It fell right on the mouthpiece and just nicked it. So what happened, so I went down to the place that do the weed for my clients, you know. And I asked them, I said, you got any mouthpieces? I said, I got one, it's a myers. Try that. So I was in a hurry and I took it and I tried it. I didn't pay for it. You tell me to try and then if you like it, you pay me for it. So I tried it. And I've been used back on the time. Well, is that the open or close lay, do you know or? No, it's a medium. It's nothing, actually. It's not an x-ray. It's just a regular stock market.

Do you have any preference on the, some of the old players, the old time players I've heard in New Orleans that even grind down, they lay up that last half inch to get it, open it up more and they think they can get a bigger tone. They said it would be harder to blow.
But they'd open it up more. No, I never did open that.
You never do it with yours to grind it down. Because if you, if you, you can, you can throw it out of a hole. I think so. Yeah.
Did you know anybody that used to do that? Work on it that way?
No, I know a guy used to do it with tenor mounties playing tennis angles.
